key_insight: 3D coupled opto-electro-thermal simulations show that lead-free MgXS3 chalcogenide perovskites can achieve high-efficiency, thermally robust solar-cell performance when thickness, doping, defects, and Sb2S3 BSF are optimized.
engineering_relevance: The study provides device-design guidance for replacing toxic Pb-based absorbers with scalable chalcogenide perovskites in realistic solar-cell architectures.
method: 3D finite-element COMSOL modeling of ZnSe/MgXS3/Sb2S3 solar cells
Self-consistent coupling of optical generation, drift-diffusion transport, and heat transfer under AM 1.5G illumination
Parametric sweep of absorber thickness, doping, defect density, and BSF effects
evidence_signal: Optimized devices reached simulated PCEs of 28.18% (MgZrS3), 26.72% (MgTiS3), and 28.16% (MgHfS3), with corresponding VOC, JSC, and FF values reported in the abstract.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based and depend on assumed material parameters, so experimental validation and defect/thermal stability in fabricated stacks remain critical.
paper_title: Numerical exploration on unveiling the photovoltaic potential of MgXS3(X = Ti, Zr, Hf) chalcogenide perovskites
